walkthroughs.body_html: A sampling frame is a list (electoral roll, school register). UK British Social Attitudes survey uses Postcode Address File. No frame = no random sample. The 1948 Truman vs Dewey US election polls famously failed due to telephone-list bias (richer respondents).

Probability samples — random, systematic, stratified — allow inference to population. Non-probability — snowball, opportunity, quota — cannot. Snowball suits hidden populations (drug users); opportunity is fast but biased; quota assigns numbers per category but selection isn't random.

Larger sample reduces sampling error but not bias. Response rates matter: BHPS achieves ~80%; many surveys <30%. Non-response bias distorts. Modern sociology often uses weighting to adjust for known imbalances (age, gender, region).
